paragraph: Abigail was feeling sad one day so she started thinking about all of the things she likes. She likes nature, video games and best of all, baked sweets. She loves to do the baking just as much as she loves eating her sweet creations. After thinking for a while, she decided to go bake a chocolate cake and bring a slice to her neighbor, Arthur. The cake turned out beautiful, moist and delicious and Abigail was so excited to share it with her neighbor. She headed over to her Arthur's house and gave him a piece. He also was feeling sad that day so he was really touched that she brought him some cake. He tried it and told her it was amazing. They both were feeling a lot better after this exchange and grateful for their friendship as neighbors.
target_clause: abigail was feeling sad one day

paragraph: All Jennifer wanted was to go to the punk rock show at the club down the street from her house. She had saved for months, waiting for the show tickets to go on sale. She was excited because three of her favorite bands were going to be there. But when the day finally came, she slept through her alarm and missed her opportunity to buy tickets -- all of them were sold out by the time she logged on! Jennifer was devastated. On the day of the show, Jennifer decided to walk down the street and just hang out outside the venue in the hopes of seeing any of the band members, or hearing the music from outside. That's when someone came up to her and said, "I have an extra ticket since my friend couldn't make it. Would you like it?" Jennifer was so happy she hugged the complete stranger! They ended up seeing the show together and becoming friends.
target_clause: all jennifer wanted was to go to the punk rock show

paragraph: Have you ever had a child?  Do you plan to?  I will say that, for us, it has been the most rewarding experiences ever.  We wanted children for a long time, and from 23 to 29 we tried and tried to get pregnant, but had no luck.  We were just about to consider in-vitro fertilization.  When we went for the check-up and the introductory meeting - we found out I was pregnant.  I have never been so elated or relieved in my whole life!   I felt so fulfilled  and alive...my husband shed tears of joy.  It was a historic moment in our story, for sure.  When she arrived, I felt peace, calmness, and fulfillment.  As I cradled her tiny body in my arms, I felt a love so fierce and strong - it almost scared me.  Throughout the years, as we have watched her grow into the electric young girl she is, I feel so proud that I have had a hand in who she become.
target_clause: have you ever had a child? do you plan to?

paragraph: I was walking along a trail one sunny day when I came across a woman sitting on the side of the trail eating lunch. We did not speak the same language, but she beckoned me to come and sit next to her, and so I did. Opening up her backpack and reaching inside, she grinned as she handed me a small container full of food and three pieces of flatbread. I opened the container and was overcome by the fragrance pouring out from underneath the edges of the lid. It was spicy, and garlicky, and bursting with coconut and lemongrass bouquets that made my nose run and my mouth water. I dipped the bread and slurped the curry under the watchful eye of the silent woman, and when I finished, she took back the container, offered me a cup of water, and began packing up her things. She walked away in the direction from which I had come, and left me happy.
target_clause: i was walking along a trail one sunny day

paragraph: I've just purchased a new home! In the yard of the new home are hostas. I'm sure you have seen a hosta at some point in your life and may not recognize the name. Hostas are large green leafy plants that enjoy shade. The are very resilient to all varieties of weather conditions with the exception of dryness and heat (just like me!). I love the new plants (and I guess the home too)! Yesterday, I propagated some new hosta growths. It was the perfect fall day for this activity. The ground was damp, the sky overcast. target_clause: i've just purchased a new home!

paragraph: In the beginning of December of 2018, a young couple agrees to adopt a dog. They've both worked exclusively with dogs and have noticed a spike in their mood when around these animals. It's almost as if they have healing powers. Facing difficulty in their personal lives, they decide to invite one into their home permanently. They start looking into apps, online listings, local shelters and they find the goofiest little thing. She's a small bulldog about 35 pounds or so, very low to the ground and has a tongue that hangs out of her mouth. It quickly becomes clear there is no way to leave this place without her. Days and weeks go by as they painstakingly wait for the adoption process to go through. Eventually, Zoey comes home. Everything is for her now, all other worries have melted away. It's as if she was a miracle.
target_clause: in the beginning of december of 2018, a young couple agrees to adopt a dog.

paragraph: Once upon a time there was a guy. He really hated the heat of summer. He moved away from the south where it was perpetually hot.  Finally Autumn came around and he was very pleased. The temperatures got cooler, it was nice to be outside, and he could wear hoodies (his favorite type of clothing). The leaves changed colors, and everywhere he looked there were pumpkins, and people drinking coffee, and the crisp sound of leaves crunching underfoot. He was very satisfied to now be living somewhere where it wasn't so hot all the time. It brought him a lot of inner peace and joy. Finally Summer had ended and his favorite time of the year was here. He would be sure to enjoy it.
target_clause: once upon a time there was a guy.

paragraph: Once upon a time there was a very joyful cow. This cow liked to eat grass in the meadow, so she always got a lot of grass. And she always ate it. And she always got enough grass. And the day dawned when the grass was out of the meadow. And the next day when the grass was back in the meadow, the cow looked a little sick, she said 'What's wrong with me? What do I have to drink to get well?' And a big old farmer went to the cow and asked what had happened. The cow said 'You must not eat so much grass, you must not eat so much grass!' But she did not get drunk or sick, and the farmer was amazed. The cow was fine when she got some water.
target_clause: once upon a time there was a very joyful cow.

paragraph: There once was a boy. He always had his head in the clouds and walked around imagining all sorts of things. Fantasies of adventure, conquering dragons, saving princesses, battling pirates, flying through space. Sometimes all at once! He had a very active imagination, he enjoyed playing, but he never had anybody that he could share it all with. The older he got, the more lonely he became. Nobody else wanted to talk about pirates and princesses anymore, they wanted to talk about stocks, careers, parties (not the fun tea parties). The world slowly turned black and white and he only had a small bit of color left. One day he stumbled on a forest lush with color! He met a girl with a paint brush painting everything! He stood in awe, she saw him and laughed. She gave him a brush and they began to paint the world together. Everyone loved them.
target_clause: there once was a boy.

paragraph: There was a little girl who felt out of place. She had a few good friends but never felt that she truly belonged to a group. As she got older these feelings got stronger and when it was time for her to begin the 6th grade at a new middle school she felt more anxious than ever about finding her place with all new people. However, on her first day of band class her fears began to slip away. She found that every day she learned more about her classmates and felt more and more that she had found her place. By the end of that year they had competed in a state-wide competition and she waited with her new group of friends to hear how they had done. They won! As they jumped up and down in celebration the girl knew that she had finally found her place.
target_clause: there was a little girl

paragraph: There was a little girl who really loved animals. She always wanted a pet but her parents always said no. For years she asked her parents for a dog or cat, or even a hamster, but they always said it's too expensive, too dirty, or too much work. One day the little girl decided that since she can't have a pet, she would go volunteer at the animal shelter so she could be around animals. She helped out there for almost a year and fell in love with one particular dog. It was a tiny white poodle. The girl always played with this dog and they got along well. One day the girl decided to ask her parents if she could adopt the dog. She was sure they would say no, but to her surprise they said she had been so generous and hard working volunteering at the shelter that she deserved a pet of her own. So the next day she took home her new best friend.
target_clause: there was a little girl who really loved animals.

paragraph: There was a puppy that was all alone.  He wandered the streets for days looking for someone to take him home with them and love them. He wanted a family of his very own.  The problem was that all of the people that he came across just did not seem to notice him at all. Everyone walked right passed him. The puppy was getting very sad and lonely.  He laid down against a building and started to whimper and cry.  Just down the street was a family.  The parents were walking with their child, a boy, who had recently gotten out of the hospital after fighting cancer and winning.  As the walked down the street the boy heard the puppy. He stopped his family and hurried over to him. He lifted him and consoled him.  His parents saw the connection the two had and asked if he wanted him. The boy said yes!  The puppy smiled with love and hope!
target_clause: there was a puppy that was all alone.

paragraph: Sally was poor her whole life, but she always knew she was smart. In school, teachers and counselors tried to advise her to go to college and get a good paying job, as this was to be the ticket to success and stability. However, over the years, Sally came to realize she couldn't ever keep a job more than a few months. Sally hated being bossed around, and putting so much personal time and energy into making other people successful. After she walked out on a job for the hundredth time, she vowed never to work for anyone again. Because she didn't have much income, she lived on beans, rice, eggs, and oatmeal for the better part of a year. But during that year, she created her own line of jewelry and accessories, and studied entrepreneurship. Sally now sells her jewelry full time and is more content than she's ever been.
target_clause: sally was poor her whole life,

paragraph: Tommy and Rob were two kids in fourth grade. They got to school each day and toiled through their classes.It always felt like the clock stopped moving after 2 PM. However, when it finally hit 3 o‚'clock both were overjoyed. Both children relished this time each day because it marked the start of their daily adventure. They would take the forest path home from school and along the way they played multiple games. Some days it was hide and seek. Others they were pioneers navigating through the jungle in search of treasure. The years would pass but that friendship and walk home from school always held a nostalgic, sacred place in their hearts whenever they would reflect back on it. The innocence of youth is fleeting and nothing is ever quite like it again.
target_clause: tommy and rob were two kids in fourth grade.

He then gave her a dozen of beautiful red roses and reminded her how lovely she is and how wonderful it was to be his wife. paragraph:
Boe the dog knew that he wasn't supposed to jump over that fence and cross the stream but that's exactly what he did.  He jumped the fence and began to cross the stream.  It was a little cooler than he thought it would be, but he remembered how much we wanted to cross the stream after those years of looking at it, and he continued.  Once he arrived on the other side, it was a strange world.  He didn't know where he was, and he was lost.  Boe wandered around aimlessly for hours, and each hour become more dire.  It seemed like some people wanted to come up to him and help.  However, Boe was too afraid of them and this situation.

Many hours passed, and the sun began to set.  Boe knew he had to get home soon and began heading to the sound of water.  He found a stream and swam across.  Then, he saw home and ran towards it.
target_clause: boe the dog knew

It was a little cooler than he thought it would be, but he remembered how much we wanted to cross the stream after those years of looking at it, and he continued.  Once he arrived on the other side, it was a strange world.  He didn't know where he was, and he was lost.  Boe wandered around aimlessly for hours, and each hour become more dire.  It seemed like some people wanted to come up to him and help.  However, Boe was too afraid of them and this situation.

Many hours passed, and the sun began to set.  Boe knew he had to get home soon and began heading to the sound of water.  He found a stream and swam across.  Then, he saw home and ran towards it.

paragraph: Christopher settled down in his usual chair at Starbucks. He set up his laptop and sipped his coffee. Someone tapped him on the shoulder. "Aren't you Chris?" said a girl he didn't know. "Yes," he said. It was strange, because he didn't know anybody in this town. "I think my sister Laurie went to school with you," she said. "We moved here about a month ago and we don't know anybody here." 'I just moved here, too," Christopher said. "Why don't you call your sister and we could all get together later?" "OK," the girl said. "I'm Janet. I have to go now. Could we meet you here at 6?" "Sure," he said. She collected her things and left; he waved to her. What a stroke of luck, he thought. He remembered Laurie, not well, but he remembered her as a nice person. He was really looking forward to meeting the girls later.
target_clause: christopher settled down in his usual chair at starbucks.

"We moved here about a month ago and we don't know anybody here." 'I just moved here, too," Christopher said. "Why don't you call your sister and we could all get together later?" "OK," the girl said. "I'm Janet. I have to go now. Could we meet you here at 6?" "Sure," he said. She collected her things and left; he waved to her. What a stroke of luck, he thought. He remembered Laurie, not well, but he remembered her as a nice person. He was really looking forward to meeting the girls later.
target_clause: but he remembered her as a nice person.

paragraph: Going to Florida is super fun. I was born in Florida, but did not grow up there. My family moved from our home in Florida when I was seven years old. Now, I go back to Florida once or twice each summer. But, I try not to go during typical summer months. I like to visit in September. That way the weather is still very warm, but the crowds of tourists are diminished. I enjoy taking my kids to the beach, and to the various other springs that Florida is famous for. We also like to do a bit of surf casting from the sand. Occasionally, we will even charter a boat and do some deep sea fishing. In order to get the most out of our Florida trips, I like to plan our activities ahead of time. It is too easy to get down to Florida and stay in the hotel room or only visit one or two sites. By planning our trip beforehand, we get to experience a lot.
target_clause: going to florida is super fun.

paragraph: I always enjoyed going shrimping and fishing with my dad. We would load up his old Ford truck and hit the road early in the morning on the weekends. His truck was that steel gray color, but the tail gate didn't match and was a faded red. He would always pop in a tape of one of his favorite classic rock bands. The windows would be down and I could smell the salt in the air the closer to the water we got. On the way I would eat a snack that my step mom had packed for us, that way I would be ready to go as soon as we got to the water. It took a while sometimes to find our spot and get everything unloaded, but once we did it was a day of fun and catching food for our family and friends.
target_clause: i always enjoyed going shrimping and fishing with my dad.

paragraph: I always enjoyed going shrimping and fishing with my dad. We would load up his old Ford truck and hit the road early in the morning on the weekends. paragraph:
I slammed  the door and walked four blocks to the convenient store. I was angry and needed to cool off. My boyfriend and I had just gotten into a fight because he always plays the blame game for even the most insignificant situations. "Can't accept criticism but you sure give it out, you tool!" I muttered angrily as I approached the store.
I grabbed the door handle and pulled it open, walking into the store. I browsed with no product in mind. I looked at chocolate, but wasn't in the mood to eat. I browsed the magazine's but was too angry to read. I grabbed a cold bottle Jasmine tea, hoping it would help me regain calm. The bored middle-aged cashier listlessly rung it up. My eye suddenly caught sight of the scratch offs. " I will take three of those". I paid and went outside, grabbed a coin and scratcged. I'd won a hundred dollars!

paragraph: I took my kids to the zoo the other week.The weather was perfect and the animals were all alert and moving around. It will be closing shortly for the season and we go a lot, about once a week, sometimes even more. We love to go see the giraffes and orangutans. My youngest son likes to feed the giraffes lettuce when they are up near the deck. The zoo is so nice, they just redid the monkey and otter exhibits and we can tell those animals are so much more happy in their newer and bigger habitats. It is nice to see the animals being treated so nicely and not cramped. We will see if we can squeeze in a few more visits this year but not sure how many we will be able to do with them both in school now. That is why we love having a membership because we don't feel the need to see it all when we go like those who have paid for the one day to go.
target_clause: i took my kids to the zoo

paragraph: I was sitting in my office when I noticed a moderately sized spider walking on the floor next to me.  I picked up a notebook and small box and crouched down to scoop the spider into the box.  I placed the notebook over the box to secure the spider inside and walked towards the door leading outside.  Once I got outside, I removed the notebook and saw the spider sitting inside the box.  I turned the box upside down and gently shook it to encourage the spider to go into the grass below.  I looked at the ground and the spider was not there.  I looked inside the box, and the spider was not there either.  I was curious as to where the spider disappeared to.  That is when I tilted the box to the side and noticed the spider repelling from the box on his web!  I smiled and then slowly lowered it to the ground and freed it in the grass.
target_clause: i was sitting in my office

I could tell the dogs knew the weather had cooled and as soon as I took out their harnesses, excitement was in the air. I do have to say that their excitement was contagious and I also felt anxious to get on the mountain and do some hiking. We finally arrive and off we go. This is the perfect day...the weather, the scenery, the wildlife!

paragraph:
It was a beautiful spring day and Jan and Petra were walking to the park.  Jan and Petra were friends since child hood and Jan was trying to cheer Petra up a bit since she was still having difficutly adjusting to the loss of her grandmother, who had passed about a month before.  They were almost to the park and were planning on having a picnic under the big oak tree 
that was near the playground.  When they got there, Jan spread out the blanket and Petra opened the picnic basket and put out the food and passed out plates.  When she looked up, Petra saw a butterfly and immediately thought that butterflies were the way passed loved ones sent a message that they were okay.  The butterfly landed next to her plate, fluttered it's wings and then flew away towards the sun.  Petra's mood brightened considerably and she enjoyed her time with Jan.
target_clause: it was a beautiful spring day

paragraph: It was a great day. Sally, Mary, Fran and I went to lunch at our favorite sandwich shop. We were there to celebrate all our birthdays. We were early for the lunch crowd, so we quickly found a table. We left our birthday gift bags and went to the counter and ordered. While we waited for our food, Mary entertained us with stories of her recent trip to Cape Cod. Fran showed us new pictures of her grandchildren that she had taken on her phone. I was content to sit and listen to all the chatter. Soon our food arrived and after a quick blessing, we dove in. Of course, the chatter continued. I was asked about my renovations on my bathroom.  I told them what I am telling everyone. I never want to renovate anything again. But I explained that the main reason was that it was taking longer than I wanted. But I am content with the results.
target_clause: it was a great day.

It‚'s raining, I just left church and was running to catch a bus home. I had to cross the road to get to the bus stop so I stood in the rain, impatiently waiting for the zebra crossing light to turn green.

paragraph:
Once fine Monday in September, a woman sat in the parking lot of her daughter's dance school.  She had just dropped her daughter off at her dance school.  It had been a struggle to get their on time, between getting the woman's other child, her son, to school safely and driving across town to get to the dance studio on time.  This mother had not eaten anything today - there was simply no time for it.  However, she will be looking forward to a good meal once her daughter's dance class was over.

As she read a book in her car, a text message appeared on her phone.  "Please come into the studio at once!!" was sent from the front office of the studio.  It turned out that the dance students wanted to show their parents their new steps.  The mother was so happy to see that her daughter was enjoy these lessons, and all of that work was worth it.
target_clause: once fine monday in september, a woman sat in the parking lot of her daughter's dance school.

paragraph: One day a girl was walking home from school. She was in a good mood because she had done very well on her test. She was excited to go and tell her mom how well she did on her test. While she was walking home she heard a noise. It was coming from behind the tree. She walked over to the tree to see what it was and she saw a little baby kitten. She decided to take the little baby kitten home to show her mom. She picked up the kitten and continued walking home. When she got home she went inside and saw her mom sitting at the table. Her mom was surprised to see the baby kitten. The girl asked her mom if she could keep the kitten. Her mom said lets ask your dad when he gets home from work and she started fixing a snack. The girl told her mom that she had a great day and did very well on her test. He mom was happy for her and fixed her some milk
target_clause: one day a girl was walking home from school.

paragraph:
Paul was satisfied with his log cabin. He had worked on it for several months, having first bought the land on the low mountain slope. He worked alone, for the most part but enlisted a friend when he needed to do some heavy lifting. His goal was to build a sustainable structure in the wilderness, away from civilization. It's not that he hated people, he just didn't know much about social cues. He considered himself a loner and always had. He did feel the need to have a dog and treated him right, even though the dog was bought to alert him to strangers entering the area, not for companionship. 

It has taken nearly a year, but his rudimentary cabin was completed. He could finally relax and enjoy himself. But he realized he got most of his joy from the work itself. Therefore, he knew he would be making constant improvements.
target_clause: paul was satisfied with his log cabin.

paragraph: There I was standing in line to receive my college diploma. The sun was beating down.  It was outside and the breeze was blowing, a truly beautiful day. I was hot and felt like I might pass out, yet I was so in the moment focused on what was happening-- something I had hoped for and dreamed about my entire life. I did horribly in high school yet now here I was standing in line graduating FIRST, literally FIRST in my college class. We had the largest graduating class and there were over 1000 people there. To hear my name read with the words summa cum laude and know that I had the highest GPA in the entire class-- seven of us tied with the GPA to be specific-- was more than I could even believe. I was always told I was a failure and yet here I was, proving to myself that I really could focus and apply myself to meet this goal. I had done it.
target_clause: there i was standing in line

paragraph: Three weeks ago a very strong hurricane was forecasted for the area I live in. Since this storm was so slow moving we were warned about it and were watching it on TV for 8 to 10 days before it's scheduled arrival. About 2 to 3 days before it was to hit I took both cars and filled them up and we went to an area designated for sand bag filling and we go the maximum 10 sand bags. I took them home and placed them where I thought they would be most needed. I picked up all the outdoor furniture and got our home as ready as possible. At the last minute the storm took a turn to the North and we got little rain and a few breezy days. This was an unexpected relief but rather short lived because there are 5 more storms out in the Atlantic and any or all could be a problem for us. Right now, however, we are in the clear.

paragraph: When my niece recently turned 11, my husband and I decided we'd like to capitalize on her waning childhood by taking her to a play known for its colorful sets and whimsical story. When her birthday arrived, we handed her a bright bouquet of edible gummy flowers with the tickets tucked in the side. Sensing a modicum of disappointment, I worried that we'd given her a boring present. Ever the polite child, however, she expressed gratitude. The night of the play came and, to our delight, she laughed throughout the entire thing. Her unbridled enthusiasm for the slapstick gags and silly costumes infected us as well. After the curtains fell, we walked to the car, recounting our favorite lines and giggling. It was lovely to see that she happen grown up yet and wasn't too cool for us. It was a special memory that I'll cherish forever.

paragraph: As a kid, I felt bad about myself, hated the way I looked. I just tried to blend in with the crowd each day and not be noticed. That changed around the time I was 16 years old, and I met Elisabeth in one of my classes at school. She was so different from anyone I had ever met. Unique, goofy, funny. Authentic. Kind and intelligent. She was beautiful, inside and out to me, and it didn't take long for me to start developing serious feelings for her. I was going to ask her out to a dance that was coming up. I remember the day came and I was so nervous, yet excited. I got to school, saw her, and the first thing she said to me was "John asked me to the dance! Can you believe it? I can't wait!'. Elisabeth dated John throughout high school, and they are married now with kids. I always wondered what could have been if I had asked her out first.
target_clause: as a kid, i felt bad about myself, hated

paragraph: It was Christmas morning and Timmy was excited to open his Christmas presents. He jumped out of bed and without even stopping to put on his slippers, he ran out of his room and down the hall.  He saw the lights from the tree glowing at the doorway that leads to the living room.  He flew into the room, expecting to find his parents and his sister, Jill, waiting for him.  First, he noticed that they weren't there where he thought they'd be, sitting with their usual excited faces like on every Christmas morning.  But once he realized the room was empty, he went on to notice that someone had in fact been there and left.  Furniture had been moved away from the fireplace. The cookies that he'd put out last night were gone. Then he found the note. "Timmy, You were a bad boy. You get nothing, and your family is going to red lobster for dinner."

Manny Mongoose used to live in a land of good hunting. Then a storm came up and swept him to an island. The islanders were friendly vegans, and offered him many plants to eat. Manny ate and ate, and it was good. But there was no meat. The longer he lived on the island, the weaker he got. 

One day, a cobra washed ashore and began to eat the islanders. The islanders didn't know what to do, since nothing had ever hunted them.

Manny had killed and eaten many cobras back in the land of good hunting. But weakened by the vegan diet, he could no longer move quickly enough to avoid the cobra's venom. The cobra bit Manny, and when the venom took effect, ate him. Then the cobra ate all the islanders.
target_clause: manny mongoose used to live in a land of good hunting.

paragraph: Murphy was on his way home from a long and exhausting day at work. On his drive towards home, his mind ran with images of what he would do when he got there. He just wanted to relax after the horrible day he had and most of all, he wanted to relax with his best friend, Willow. Willow was a dog he had rescued 6 years ago and he couldn't imagine life without her now. She was the one thing in life that could make him smile and lift him up out of a funk. His spirits started to rise as he walked up the steps to the house, excited to see her. He opened the door and she wasn't there to greet him. He called for her...nothing. The house was completely silent. Starting to panic a bit, he dropped his laptop bag and ran room to room through the house calling her name as he did. When he reached the bedroom, he saw her there, on the bed, lifeless.
target_clause: murphy was on his way home from a long and exhausting day at work.

paragraph: Once there was a little boy names Jacob who was born to a drug addicted mother and an alcoholic father. The mother gave birth to Jacob at home, and poor little Jacob was given no immediate care after birth. Jacob's mother took as good a care of him as she could, but after 6 months, CPS investigated Jacob's family, and he was removed from his parents care. The first foster family was almost as bad as his birth parents, and Jacob would be left in soiled diapers and almost starved. When he was placed into a second foster family, he was given a second chance at life, and was given to a family who would take care of him. He was eventually adopted by this family. However, at age 16, he committed suicide, after not being able to forgive his birth parents.
target_clause: once there was a little boy names jacob

paragraph: One July 4th I went out to stay at my parents place out in the suburbs. They were away and it was just my girlfriend and I. I was happy to see my beloved dog, a german shepard. She seemed a bit off one night, however I fed her some Kentucky Fried Chicken that someone had picked up and she loved it. The next morning she was incredibly ill and could not move, she was in a terribly state as she had been not doing well physically for a long time and could not really walk on her own. That morning I knew it was time and we wrapped her up in a blanket and had to take her to the doctor to be put to sleep. I will always remember her and that time. It was one of the toughest things I have ever had to do.
target_clause: one july 4th i went out to stay at my parents place out in the suburbs.

Everything was going well , but now it has begun to dry up. I don't know what to do this year. It looks pretty unlikely that we will travel this year. Working all year and thinking about this trip and knowing we may not go has been very hard to accept. Hopefully things will pick up on Mturk and I can earn the money needed. It really sucks to be this poor. It really does!
target_clause: working all year and thinking about this trip

paragraph: Recently, a friend of the family passed away. She is related to my niece and nephew. Unfortunately my niece and nephew are getting use to this kind of thing. Their mom and dad have both passed away. They have had friends pass away form cancer and they are barely in their teenage years. I feel so bad for them. People are dropping dead around them and leaving these kids on their own. I try to be there for them, but I have not raised them and they don't know me very well. We would all be here to support these kids, but none of us have been given the chance to do so. It has been very sad for all of us involved. The kids will be coming up from Florida and we will be able to see them and see how they are handling things. Could you imagine being that age and losing so may people. It's heartbreaking. I feel so bad for these kids.
target_clause: recently, a friend of the family passed away.

paragraph: The Winter morning was dark and cold. That bitter cold that freezes the hairs in your nostrils. Sitting in the driveway, its mechanical odometer reading over 230,000 miles, was the old pickup truck. Through over twenty years and several owners, this old truck has soldiered on through many a Winter. However on this morning, it would finally fall. Upon starting up, the dry rotted oil line finally let go. Oil began to spray onto the driveway. The owner, eager to return to their warm shelter, was unaware of this. The old engine began to struggle as it starved for oil. Its idle grew rough and labored. Its owner, now inside, could not hear the engine as it began to tear itself apart. This old truck's next home would be a scrap yard, where it would be robbed of its parts while it continued to rust away.
target_clause: the winter morning was dark and cold.

Upon starting up, the dry rotted oil line finally let go. Oil began to spray onto the driveway. The owner, eager to return to their warm shelter, was unaware of this. The old engine began to struggle as it starved for oil. Its idle grew rough and labored. Its owner, now inside, could not hear the engine as it began to tear itself apart. This old truck's next home would be a scrap yard, where it would be robbed of its parts while it continued to rust away.
target_clause: as it began to tear itself apart.

One day, the man's friend noticed that he was no longer speaking. He seemed to struggle to find words to express his thoughts, needs, and feelings. His wife took him to a doctor who told her the man was ill and would get worse over time. Eventually, the man would no longer be able to take care of himself. His body and mind would forget everything. He would forget not only her and their children, but also all the little things a person's body does automatically. Because he was a very smart man, the progression would be slow and last many, many years. She was devastated, but did her best to take care of him as he lost himself and she lost him. But she still had their children.
target_clause: and she lost him.

paragraph: There was a girl who lived in a small town in the Netherlands. She felt so happy because she had the most loving father. He was an only parent and took care of her every need. He would cook for the little girl, give her presents, tuck her in at night, and scare any bad monsters out from under her bed. She loved her father so very much and knew that he would always keep her safe. He had big, broad shoulders to lift her, great wide arms to hug her, and great, big hands to wipe her tears. The little girl knew her father was the best father in the whole, wide world. Suddenly, the little girl started shaking. Someone was shaking her to wake her up. She opened her eyes. Her father was gone. She was back in the orphanage where she lived.

paragraph: There was a little boy named Jerry who lived in an impoverished rural area of the US.  He was one of 3 kids, but his home life was pretty dysfunctional -- his Mommy and Daddy were always fighting, and were always worried about money.  In fact, several days out of the week, Jerry and his siblings wouldn't have anything to eat.  His daddy would disappear for hours (which turned into days) because he said he needed to go to "work" - but there was never any paycheck to show for all that time and effort.  Sometimes Jerry's daddy would get drunk and yell, and his mommy would get drunk and yell back at him, and Jerry would hide in the single bedroom and cry.  One day, Jerry's daddy said he was going out to buy some groceries and a pack of cigarettes, and would be back within the hour.  But he never came home.  Jerry never saw him again.
target_clause: there was a little boy named jerry

paragraph: A person interviewed for a job that they were interested in. It wasn't their dream job, but it was a job they liked the idea of and were hopeful about. They felt it would be better than they're current alternatives. They purchased a new shirt and pants for the interview. They practiced questions with a friend that they thought they may be asked and even allowed the friend to make up questions. They were well prepared for the interview and showed up on the day of. They sat down to interview and felt it went well. Unfortunately however they were not hired for the job. This disappointed them but fortunately it wasn't for their dream job.

paragraph: A thin sheet of ice stuck to the window of the storefront where Jessie lived. Jessie had lived in the storefront ever since Granny took ill and was left in the house. After failing to wake her up for a few days, Jessie finally decided to leave the home that he knew as a child. A young man of his teen years who had never knew a world outside of Granny, was suddenly left alone to discover the "new world." Jessie stumbled upon the desolate storefront one night while searching food in any dumpster he could find. Although it was small, cold, and cluttered with someone's long-forgotten belongings, Jessie now had a new place to call home. Jessie blew steam onto the frozen window as he watched people he did not know hustle to destinations, maybe to meet friends or find a new love. In Jessie's heart, he knew there was no one looking for him.
target_clause: a thin sheet of ice stuck to the window of the storefront where jessie lived.

After failing to wake her up for a few days, Jessie finally decided to leave the home that he knew as a child. A young man of his teen years who had never knew a world outside of Granny, was suddenly left alone to discover the "new world." Jessie stumbled upon the desolate storefront one night while searching food in any dumpster he could find. Although it was small, cold, and cluttered with someone's long-forgotten belongings, Jessie now had a new place to call home. Jessie blew steam onto the frozen window as he watched people he did not know hustle to destinations, maybe to meet friends or find a new love. In Jessie's heart, he knew there was no one looking for him.

paragraph: A troll lived alone in a very large cave deep in the mountains, with no friends.  Sometimes adventurers would visit but no matter how much he tried to befriend them, they started shouting about "smiting evil" and "driving the pestilence of your wicked ways from this land."  And then they attacked.  They always attacked.  Due to his troll anatomy he could understand the humans and dwarves perfectly but couldn't seem to speak their language.  Rupert finally had a flash of insight and decided that since humans and dwarves seemed to talk of little else but treasure, a gift must be the way to friendship.  He traded his nicest club to a goblin for a shiny copper locket.  When he offered it to the next adventurer with a hearty grin, his heart sank as he heard ‚ÄúI'd recognize that anywhere!  What have you done with my Matilda you evil brute?!‚Äù  His heart sank as he realized he would die alone.
target_clause: a troll lived alone in a very large cave deep in the mountains,

paragraph: As John woke up, he couldn't shake the feeling that something was wrong. He had a knot in his stomach and he found it hard to swallow. He hated days like this, when his anxiety took over for no apparent reason. His life has been going so well, there was no reason for him to feel the way that he did. He always feared that this feeling was somewhat of a precognition of bad things to come. Most of his life when he felt like this bad things did come his way, he always thought that it was a higher power at work and he somehow knew that the higher power was going to torture him. Sure enough, he walked into his bathroom and found his favorite fish, Fishy McFish Face, floating dead at the top of the fish tank. He was hoping this was the end of it.
target_clause: as john woke up,

paragraph: Brittany was the best cat I ever had, and believe me, I‚'ve had dozens of cats in my lifetime. She was a purebred brown Burmese cat with bright gold eyes, silky brown short hair and a small, muscular body. I experienced many of Brittany‚'s life stages with her, raising her from a small kitten through motherhood and beyond. While living in north Georgia, I adopted Brittany from a breeder in north Florida, which was about 350 miles away. Having had many types of cats, I knew I wanted a Burmese so I was willing to travel to get her and it was so worth it. She was waiting at home when I brought my young daughter home from an Eastern European orphanage in the early 1990‚'s. They remained fast friends throughout my daughter‚'s childhood. Thankfully, my daughter was away at a sleepover when Brittany passed quietly in my lap after a pancreatic event.

paragraph: I think I have a migraine headache. Looking out of the window, nothing seems interesting. I wanted to call my sister, Ruth, and tell her that I would not be coming to her house as I promised but the headache was so painful that making the effort to make the call was like work. Thank God this is a Saturday. I did not need to go to work. I could imagine my supervisor, Donald, barking at me and asking me why my migraines and problems were not left at home. "We pay you to work and you should be putting your best at work," I can imagine him saying as he barked. Behind me, the television was showing the news. Just when I was decided on going to the bedroom to lie down, the phone rang. Ruth!

I decide I will take my treasures to the food court to celebrate my good fortune. I get my normal meal from TacoBell, a stake quesadilla, Mexican pizza, and a Baja Blast. paragraph: It wasn't the first time the two had been separated, but this time was definitely different.  Connor was on a plane heading west; Lucy was on a plane heading east.  Both knew when they'd likely see each other next, but even then things wouldn't be like they'd been before.  Connor was heading to UCLA, to study theater and English.   Lucy, his twin sister, was heading to Duke to study political science.  Connor wanted to be an actor while Lucy wanted to eventually go into politics.  Connor always joked that they both wanted to be actors; he was just doing it more honestly.  That type of playful joking between siblings had gone on since they were young, but only now did he consciously think about it, even miss it, knowing that his sister, so indelibly connected to him, was starting her own life without him, and he without her.

paragraph: Johnny was an upset man, sitting in his dreary room, eating from his dull bowl of cold porridge, and if you couldn't tell already, was pretty depressed. All he wanted was for his identity as a human being be anything other than the "kid that's depressed all the time". He used to enjoy being that kid, but believe him, That got old rather quickly for him. What else could he possibly do? After he's spent all this time being "The kid that's depressed", could he ever really find out how to be anyone else? There's already a "kid who's happy all the time" and "kid who's mad all the time", so it's not like he can swap to those. Unfortunately, he's really just stuck the way he is, and over time, grew to accept it.

paragraph: Last week I was walking with my dog outside on the streets of my city. We came across a pidgeon who was grounded. She was still alive, but very weak and could not fly or even stand up. I didn't want her to lay there in the gutter in misery, so I found a cardboard box and brought her to my apartment. I figured she would at least be warm and as comfortable as possible there in her last hours. Figuring she might be thirsty, I offered her a drink of water and surprisingly she took it. I didn't have many groceries in the house but I did have a leftover doughnut that I offered her. She ignored it at first, but within an hour or two started pecking at it. I was surprised to find her still alive the next morning. I read online that pidgeons eat dove food, so I bought some of that, some grit for digestion, and some bedding for her box.
target_clause: last week i was walking with my dog outside on the streets of my city.

paragraph: Mary had a bad day at work. Her coworker didn't help her with a difficult project. Her boss discovered an error in her work and reprimanded her for it. She got through the day by counting the hours and minutes until she got home. Once she got there, she'd get to hug her husband, pet her dog, and eat the leftovers from the dinner she'd had the night before at her favorite restaurant. It was Peking duck, a dish she did not eat often, because it was pretty expensive. Finally, it was time to go home to her family and her yummy meal. When Mary arrived, there was nobody there to greet her. Her husband had left a note saying he had gone to a friend's house and he'd taken their dog with him. The note also said "I ate the duck because I didn't want it to go to waste." Mary was very disappointed and even cried a little.

paragraph:
Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved animals. He had received a pet dog as a gift for his fourth birthday---about two or so odd years ago. He had named his dog "Peanut Butter" after his favorite snack. He and Peanut Butter went everywhere together.

One summer day, the little boy decided to take a walk with his dog by the bay. The weather was perfect---the sun was shining, and there was a steady breeze that helped keep the heat off your skin. The afternoon was going as any other when all of a sudden, Peanut Butter saw a seagull in the water. Excitedly, the dog jumped out into the ocean, making a big splash. The little boy was horrified as his best friend floated away, forgetting all about him and instead focusing on the seagull.
target_clause: once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved animals.

paragraph: One day I woke up feeling mildly anxious in anticipation of a doctor's appointment. I haven't gone in years, so I wasn't sure what I was going to expect. I grew up very healthy and happy. I just knew that going to the doctor made me unhappy. I am more of an introvert, so really  any type of interaction with people I don't know can make me feel stressed out. I keep alot of my concerns inside, but I think that is what causes my unhappiness. Sometimes I wish I could be different, but than I wouldn't be true to myself. I am who I am and have to trust myself and know that God made me the way I am for reason. I think traits can be passed down through families generation after generation. My grandma and I were alike in that way. I miss her because we can relate. She lived a happy life. She was married and had two children and lived to be 94.
target_clause: one day i woke up feeling mildly anxious

paragraph: Steph's grandma knew that her time was running out. Her husband had already died so she had been lonely for a while now. She still enjoys the things that she usually enjoys, but her attention span is much shorter. She always loved watching television, but it is hard for her to enjoy it as much as she used to. With the help of Steph, she now knows how to use a computer. Given grandma's left-wing politics, browsing the internet does not give her much joy. She is a very kind person and does not like hearing about what's going on in the world. She listens to podcasts but on 1.5x speed, because she knows she doesn't have enough time to listen to all the different podcasts out there at normal speeds.
target_clause: steph's grandma knew that her time was running out.

paragraph: There was a thirteen year old boy named Sam who always wanted a pet growing up. His parents would never entertain the idea because they were afraid he would not take proper care of it. Since today was his birthday, and he finally entered the teen stage, his mother decided to surprise him with a Golden Retriever puppy. Sam was overjoyed and thankful; he promised his parents that he would do his best to take care of the puppy. Sam decided to name the puppy Scooter and played with him everyday for hours for the next few years. However, once Sam got older and received more responsibilities such as finding a job to help pay for his car and phone bill, Sam did not have as much time to spend with Scooter. The choir from Coral Reef Senior High has held national prestige and merit for quite some time, so needless to say those who make it on this stage have the ability to advance their careers in music in musically gifted college. Furthermore, there was a field trip arranged to go to Disney World in Orlando, Florida about 4 days ago from the actual recital performance. After the incident, four choir boys were heavily affected by the smoke, thus disqualifying them from the choir recital.

paragraph:
We have a lonely neighbor.  He is an older man whose wife is away a lot caring for their grandchild in another town.  This leave shim at home alone.  He's had health issues and so has is wife but she insists that she's needed elsewhere and rarely spends time with her husband.  
Unfortunately this man likes to visit with anybody that will give him the time of day.  If we're out in the yard working he will come over and want to chat about politics mainly.  We're always nice to him but he never gets the hint that we're not interested in his political views.  We kindly listen and say, "that's nice but we have work to do."  he then ambles back to his house and watches out the window for his next chance to socialize with any neighbor that ventures into their yard.  He's very lonely.
target_clause: we have a lonely neighbor.

We have a lonely neighbor.  He is an older man whose wife is away a lot caring for their grandchild in another town.  This leave shim at home alone.  He's had health issues and so has is wife but she insists that she's needed elsewhere and rarely spends time with her husband.  
Unfortunately this man likes to visit with anybody that will give him the time of day.  If we're out in the yard working he will come over and want to chat about politics mainly.  We're always nice to him but he never gets the hint that we're not interested in his political views.  We kindly listen and say, "that's nice but we have work to do."  he then ambles back to his house and watches out the window for his next chance to socialize with any neighbor that ventures into their yard.  He's very lonely.
target_clause: that ventures into their yard. he's very lonely.

paragraph: When I was young we had a dog named Sparky. Sparky was some sort of terrier mix and he was always happy and excited about life. The only real trouble he ever got into was going to the neighbor's house and stealing their chickens. Because of this, Sparky had to be kept on a dog run on our property. My parents did not want a dog living in the house so Sparky had to stay outside. Sparky did not seem to mind this at all. Except for when the cat would come near his dog run...Sparky wanted to be friends with the cat, but the cat was more interested in swatting at Sparky's nose. Sparky was a great dog and I really liked him. After a bad winter, it was decided that we could no longer keep Sparky because he got too cold outside and my parents still didn't want him in the house. We had to take him to our local animal shelter. I was so sad to not have a dog anymore, but now that I am older I understand why he had to be given up. I really hope he went to a good home where he was cared for and lived out the rest of his life in a warm house.
target_clause: when i was young

paragraph: You finish your session and when Wendy, your therapist, stands up you feel a weird maternal kick, like you should hug her, but of course you don't. She walks you to the door, and pats your back gently as she lets you out. She tells you she'll see you Tuesday, and then you're back inside that waiting room, a silent couple glancing up from a shared magazine, and you just look away and head to the exit. You have no reason to start crying, but before you even make it to your car, you're blinking fast, your vision blurring, and you sit down inside and inhale sharply, rubbing your eyes. It passes after a moment, so quick to come on and so quick to fade. You make yourself take a few deep breathes until you stop feeling like a raw, exposed nerve, and you finally turn on the car so you can go home.
target_clause: you finish your session

paragraph: Cloudy and foggy - such was the condition of the sky for Mark's birthday, but he wouldn't have it any other way. Mark liked cloudy days; it gave him an odd sense of satisfaction, like droplets of water hitting a robust campfire. He'd long since moved out of his parents' home, and life had been tumultuous ever since, but today, he could take a little solace in the fact that it was all about himself. Letting the drapes fall back across the window, Mark sauntered over to his computer desk and started casually typing. He didn't need much; his studio apartment, while cramped, fit a twin bed and his computer desk, and ample wall space, decorated in colorful anime posters and fantastically dressed humans and other creatures. This was his zone, and he was happy to spend the day enjoying it just as he wanted, no matter how young or old he was.

He'd long since moved out of his parents' home, and life had been tumultuous ever since, but today, he could take a little solace in the fact that it was all about himself. Letting the drapes fall back across the window, Mark sauntered over to his computer desk and started casually typing. He didn't need much; his studio apartment, while cramped, fit a twin bed and his computer desk, and ample wall space, decorated in colorful anime posters and fantastically dressed humans and other creatures. This was his zone, and he was happy to spend the day enjoying it just as he wanted, no matter how young or old he was.
target_clause: as he wanted, no matter how young or old he was.

paragraph: There were once two chicken farmers who hated each other because they were neighbors who shared a fence but also bitter rivals. One farmer raised red-feathered chickens, and the other farmer raised white-feathered chickens. The chickens didn't know any better, though, to them the farmers were just strange featherless creatures who would sometimes make loud noises at each other over the fence and wake the chickens up from their sleep.  One day, one of the farmers discovered that the eggs on his farm were gold-colored. Very strange, because up until then they'd been bone white. The other farmer discovered the same thing on his side of the fence.  Each farmer took the eggs to the market and sold twice the amount they usually did. Turned out there was a hole in their fence and their chickens had been breeding with the ones on the other side.
target_clause: there were once two chicken farmers

paragraph: A man was looking for his can opener because he was hungry. He looked everywhere and could not find it anywhere. He needed to get that can of Billy Bo's Famous Baked Beans. The man grabbed a random screwdriver he had laying in his kitchen junk drawer and started hitting the top of the can with it in hopes of prying the top open. He tried and tried but the Beans were just too strong. Out of frustration he started swinging the Bean can into things around the kitchen. Pots and pans were falling over his chairs were amiss the counter was chipped, the clock fell off the wall. He then set the Bean can on the counter and disappeared for a moment. When the man came back he had his trusty shotgun. He smirked at the cans as he raised it. The top of the can gently came open. The man was lowered the gun, he was relieved.
target_clause: a man was looking for his can opener

paragraph:
I went to the aquarium in Monterey with my grand-daughter last weekend.  We drove there in about two hours and checked in a hotel by the aquarium.  My grand-daughter was really excited, she is 6 years old.  This was our first trip together for just the two of us.  
We woke up early and got breakfast by the hotel. We could smell the ocean air.  Lucy (my grand-daughter) was practically jumping up and down.  She really didn't want to eat breakfast until the server brought out their speciality, dolphin and whale pancakes.  It had whip cream on it with a cherry on top. She really loved that. 
After breakfast, we walked down to the aquarium.  She was skipping the whole way there.   We got there and joined a tour for kids.  Lucy and the other kids were able to touch the sea anemones and the other sea creatures.  She loved it.
target_clause: i went to the aquarium in monterey with my grand-daughter last weekend.

paragraph: Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella.  She really loved eating chocolate candy bars.  One day, she was skipping through the woods on her way home from school.  She was eating a chocolate candy bar and accidentally dropped it.  She started to cry and feel sad.  She decided that she would just continue to carry her dirty candy bar home and ask her mom what to do.  A short time later she arrived home.  Her mother was in the kitchen and asked Bella how her day at school was.  Bella told her mom that school was fine but she dropped her candy bar in the forest.  Her mom was understanding and took a look at the candy bar.  She simply brushed off the dirt and told her daughter to go ahead and finish eating it.  Bella joyfully finished her candy bar.
target_clause: once upon a time there was a little girl named bella.

paragraph: Linda decided to go on a walk Monday. She thought it might brighten her mood a little since it was a Monday, after all. She put on her exercise clothes and her walking shoes. She decided to bring her dog Jake with her since he hadn't been walked today. She grabbed her cell phone and keys, put on Jake's leash, and they headed out the door. Walking down the neighborhood street, Linda noticed how quiet it was. She didn't see anyone else walking around. Linda and Jake kept walking, and she smiled as she saw how excited Jake was to be outside. She heard some birds singing and chirping away, and she caught a glimpse of a squirrel scampering away with something in its mouth. Soon it was time to head back home, and she did so with a smile on her face, feeling a lot less stressed.

paragraph:
A young girl was anxiously waiting for her Dad to get home. She loved running towards him and leaping into his arms. He always caught her and lifted her skyward and said "How's my girl today?
"  Unfortunately, today her Dad had to work late. His boss threw a project for an important client at him near quitting time,
and, he was not the kind of man you wanted to disappoint. A different person at work had recently messed up a job for that client, and so it was important to get this one right. Dad felt like he had no choice - he had to stay late and finish the job. His little girl would just have to be disappointed this evening. Even her favorite - grilled cheese sandwiches that her Mom made for her couldn't cheer her up. She grabbed her favorite teddy bear and went to bed early.
target_clause: a young girl was anxiously waiting for her dad to get home.

paragraph:
At the age of 43 he made the decision to jump out of plane. The idea scared the shit out of him but the reward of finally being like a real man was worth it. So all geared up away he flew -  The plane's door open during the whole flight. Trying hard not to gag in front of the everyone he approached the door once they were above the clouds. Don't think you coward! Just jump. What was the worst that could happen? Living like this is far worse than shoot not opening, he thought.
So he jumped and fell towards the Earth at 120 mph.
He felt at peace as he fell. Frantic thoughts did not cross his mind as one might think.
Just peace. When he hit the ground and stood up tears filled his eyes.
he would never be a real man.
target_clause: at the age of 43 he made the decision to jump out of plane.

paragraph: Ignorak looked forward to his upcoming fishing trip. Each year he would commence the Summer season with a trip to a nearby stream that was filled with lively Trout. He liked to go flyfishing, and he had honed his technique over many years and many fishing trips. This year had been a particularly difficult year for Ignorak as he had worked very hard all year with little time for resting or fishing. He looked forward with great anticipation to some well deserved time doing his favorite activity. The day finally came and he was off to the stream. After a short but strenuous hike he decided to take a break. Ignorak thought he must be getting older because the hike seemed to take a toll on him like never before. It was only while resting that he realized he had already passed where the stream had been. Unfortunately, it had dried up.
target_clause: ignorak looked forward to his upcoming fishing trip.

paragraph: There was a boy who always wanted a pet goldfish. He always wanted a pet but his parents thought that having a pet was too much work and responsibly for the boy to handle.
